Triply Robust Panel (TROP) estimator

Source: R/trop.R
trop.Rd

trop() calculates the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) with the TROP estimator of Athey, Imbens, Qu, and Viviano (2026). A cell is one unit in one period. For each treated cell, a model calculates the outcome without the treatment. The model has two-way fixed effects and a low-rank term with a nuclear-norm penalty, and it uses only untreated cells. Unit weights decrease with the distance between the outcome history of a unit and the treated unit. Time weights decrease with the distance in periods.

Usage

trop(
  data,
  outcome,
  treatment,
  unit,
  time,
  method = c("local", "global"),
  lambda = NULL,
  grid = trop_grid(),
  cv_cells = NULL,
  n_placebo = 200L,
  placebo_size = 1L,
  max_cycles = 10L,
  se = c("bootstrap", "none"),
  n_boot = 200L,
  resample = c("stratified", "controls"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  ci = c("normal", "percentile"),
  control = trop_control(),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format with one row for each unit and period.

outcome, treatment, unit, time

Column names as strings. The treatment must be 0 or 1. Outcomes can be NA. The fits do not use these cells.

method

Use "local" or "global". Refer to the section Methods.

lambda

The tuning parameters as a named numeric vector or a named list with the names time, unit, and nn. If lambda is NULL, cross-validation selects the tuning parameters from grid.

grid

The tuning grids from trop_grid().

cv_cells

For the local method, the number of untreated cells in a random sample for the leave-one-out criterion. If cv_cells is NULL, the criterion uses all untreated cells, as in Eq. 5 of the paper.

n_placebo, placebo_size

For the global method, the number of placebo sets and the number of untreated units in each set. The defaults are the values of the Python package from the authors: 200 sets of 1 unit.

max_cycles

The maximum number of cycles of the coordinate search.

se

Use "bootstrap" for bootstrap standard errors or "none" for no standard errors.

n_boot

The number of bootstrap draws.

resample

Use "stratified" or "controls". Refer to the section Inference.

conf_level

The confidence level of the interval.

ci

Use "normal" or "percentile". The normal interval is the estimate plus or minus a normal quantile times the bootstrap standard error. The percentile interval uses quantiles of the bootstrap draws. Refer to the section Inference.

control

The solver options from trop_control().

seed

An optional integer seed for the sampled cells, the placebo sets, and the bootstrap. The function does not change the state of the random number generator in the R session.

Value

An object of class trop. It is a list with these elements and with other elements:

  • estimate: the ATT.

  • std.error, conf.low, and conf.high: the bootstrap standard error and the confidence interval.

  • tau: a matrix with the effect for each treated cell.

  • lambda: the tuning parameters.

  • cv: the results of the cross-validation, or NULL for fixed tuning parameters.

  • boot: the bootstrap draws.

  • timing: the time in the C code and the total time, in seconds.

Methods

  • The local method (method = "local") is the estimator of Eq. 12 and Algorithm 2 of the paper. Each treated cell has its own unit weights, time weights, and fit. The leave-one-out criterion of Eq. 4 and Eq. 5 selects the tuning parameters. The coordinate search follows footnote 2 of the paper. You can use this method for block, staggered, and general designs.

  • The global method (method = "global") is the estimator of the Python package from the authors. It calculates one fit for a block design. The time weights decrease with the distance from the center of the treated block. The unit weights decrease with the distance from the average treated unit before the treatment. Placebo cross-validation on untreated units selects the tuning parameters. The coordinate search starts at the means of the grids.

Designs

In a block design, all treated units start the treatment in the same period and stay treated to the end of the panel. In a staggered design, the start periods are different, but the treatment does not stop. In a general design, the treatment stops for one or more units.

Inference

The unit bootstrap of Algorithm 3 of the paper gives the standard error. The bootstrap keeps the tuning parameters fixed. With resample = "stratified", the bootstrap draws treated and untreated units separately. With resample = "controls", the treated units do not change. The standard error is the standard deviation of the draws.

The default interval is the normal interval with this standard error, as in the bootstrap variance of the paper. With ci = "percentile", the interval comes from quantiles of the draws, as in the Python package from the authors. A percentile interval is less accurate with a small number of draws. The paper also says that the bootstrap is correct only with many treated units. Thus, the function gives a warning message for a bootstrap with fewer than 5 treated units.

Limits of the triple robustness result

Theorem 5.1 of the paper gives a bound for the bias. The bound is the product of three terms: the unit imbalance, the time imbalance, and the bias of the regression adjustment. The proof uses fixed weights, and it is only for a block design. For a staggered or general design, the function calculates the estimator, but the bound has no proof. Thus, the function gives a warning message for these designs.

References

Athey, S., Imbens, G. W., Qu, Z., and Viviano, D. (2026). Triply Robust Panel Estimators. Journal of Applied Econometrics. doi:10.1002/jae.70061 .

Examples

sim <- trop_simulate(n_units = 20, n_periods = 12, n_treated = 5,
                     n_post = 3, effect = 1, seed = 1)
fit <- trop(sim, "y", "d", "unit", "time",
            lambda = c(time = 0.2, unit = 0.5, nn = 0.5),
            n_boot = 50, seed = 1, control = trop_control(threads = 1))
fit
#> Triply Robust Panel (TROP) estimate
#>   Method: local | Design: block | Units: 20 | Periods: 12 | Treated cells: 15
#>   ATT: 1.119  (SE 0.202, 95% CI 0.7228 to 1.515)
#>   lambda: time = 0.2, unit = 0.5, nn = 0.5
